definition_zh: 温暖的；暖和的；热情的；动词：使暖和、加热
definition_en: fairly hot in a pleasant way, friendly and enthusiastic, or to make something slightly hotter
core_image: 双手捧住一杯刚倒的热茶，指尖一点点回暖
scene: 冬天的厨房窗户起了雾，灶上的水正冒着热气。She wrapped both hands around the warm cup and stopped shivering.
sceneCN: 这里 warm 是「温暖的、暖和的」（第 1 个义项：温度适中而令人舒适）；句意为她双手捧住暖和的杯子，不再发抖。捧着热杯回温的感觉，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 形容词：温暖的；暖和的；热情的、亲切的
动词：使暖和；加热；变得热情

derivatives.zh: 加名词后缀 -th 构成，义为「温暖；热情」
加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「温暖地；热情地」
由比较级转为名词，义为「加热器；暖手器」
加 -ing 构成，义为「变暖；加温」

senses.title: Pleasantly hot
senses.titleCN: 温暖的：温度舒服地偏高
senses.definition: fairly hot, especially in a way that feels pleasant rather than uncomfortable
senses.definitionCN: 温度较高，尤其令人舒适而不难受
senses.example: The bread was still warm from the oven.
senses.exampleCN: 面包刚从炉子里出来，还热着。
senses.why: Old English wearm described a moderate heat, and the word has always kept that comfort, not the extreme.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 wearm 指适中的热度，这个词一直保留着舒适感，而不指极端。

senses.title: Of clothing or shelter
senses.titleCN: 保暖的：衣物或住处不易散失热量
senses.definition: keeping the body heat in, as of clothes, rooms or bedding
senses.definitionCN: 能留住体温的，如衣服、房间或被褥
senses.example: Take a warm coat; the wind is sharp tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 带上件厚外套，今晚风很刺骨。
senses.why: The same moderate heat is held close to the body, so the adjective moves from air to clothing.
senses.whyCN: 同一种适中的热度被留在身体旁边，于是形容词从空气转移到衣物上。

senses.title: Friendly and enthusiastic
senses.titleCN: 热情的：态度亲切而热烈
senses.definition: showing friendliness, affection or enthusiasm
senses.definitionCN: 表现出友善、亲近或热忱
senses.example: They gave the visitors a warm welcome at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在门口热情地欢迎来访者。
senses.why: Warmth in the body became warmth in manner: a person who makes you comfortable is metaphorically warm.
senses.whyCN: 身上的温暖变成了态度上的温暖：让人感到舒适的人，在比喻意义上就是 warm。

senses.title: To make slightly hotter
senses.definition: to make something warmer, or to become warmer
senses.definitionCN: 使某物变暖，或自身变暖
senses.example: Warm the milk gently before adding the honey.
senses.exampleCN: 加蜂蜜之前先把牛奶稍稍加热。
senses.why: The adjective turns into the action that produces it: heat is applied a little at a time.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成产生它的动作：热被一点一点地加上去。

senses.title: To become friendly toward
senses.titleCN: 变得喜欢：对某人某事生出好感
senses.definition: in phrases like warm to, to begin to like or feel friendly toward something
senses.definitionCN: 用于 warm to 等短语，指开始喜欢或对某事产生好感
senses.example: The audience warmed to her after the second song.
senses.exampleCN: 第二首歌之后，观众开始喜欢上她。
senses.why: Friendliness is again heat, but now rising slowly, as a cold room warms up.
senses.whyCN: 友善再度成了热，只不过这次是慢慢升起的，像一间冷屋子渐渐暖起来。

intro.en: Warm is an old Germanic word, and its relatives run all through northern Europe.
intro.cn: warm 是古老的日耳曼语词，它的同源词遍布北欧各语言。

items.en: Wearm meant 'warm, not cold', and also appeared in compounds for warm-hearted feeling.
items.cn: wearm 意为「暖的、不冷的」，也出现在表示热心的复合词中。

items.en: The root is reconstructed as a word for being warm; German warm and Dutch warm are exact cognates.
items.cn: 这个词根被重构为「温暖」之义；德语 warm 与荷兰语 warm 是精确同源词。

items.en: Deeper connections to Latin formus 'warm' are debated, and the further origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 它与拉丁语 formus「暖的」之间更深的关系仍有争议，更早的来源不确定。

items.en: The spelling settled as warm, and the verb use, to warm something, was already common.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 warm，动词用法「使暖和」当时已很常见。

items.en: Idioms extended the word: warm up for exercise, warm to an idea, a warm welcome.
items.cn: 习语进一步扩展了它：warm up 热身、warm to 产生好感、warm welcome 热情欢迎。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers temperature words close in shape; the near-meaning group gathers degrees and kinds of heat.
note.cn: 形近组收形状相近的温度词；近义组收不同程度与不同性质的热。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being warm, and for friendly feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「温暖；热情」，指暖的性质与友善情感。

entries.definition: A device or garment that keeps something warm; also the comparative.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指保暖的器具或衣物；也是比较级形式。

entries.definition: The adverb for doing something in a warm or friendly way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「温暖地；热情地」。

entries.definition: Gentle exercise before a sport or performance.
At a high temperature, often uncomfortable; far stronger than warm.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「热的」，温度高且常令人不适，比 warm 强得多。

entries.definition: Only slightly warm, and by extension unenthusiastic.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「微温的」，引申为「不热心的」。

entries.definition: Snug and comfortable; the feeling of warmth rather than its degree.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「舒适暖和的」，侧重感受而非温度。

entries.definition: Made hot deliberately; also describes an angry argument.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「加热的」，也形容激烈的争论。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English wearm and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语 wearm，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: warm sits between cool and hot: pleasant heat, not a burn.
normal.cn: warm 位于 cool 与 hot 之间：是舒服的热，不会烫。

normal.en: A warm welcome borrows the body's comfort for the manners.
normal.cn: a warm welcome 借身体的舒适来形容待客之道。

normal.en: Warm up first, or the muscles will complain.
normal.cn: 先 warm up 热身，否则肌肉会抱怨。

normal.en: Lukewarm adds a lukewarm middle: only slightly warm, and not keen.
normal.cn: lukewarm 在中间加了一层：只是微温，也不太热心。

normal.en: Warmth is the noun; warmly is how a warm person acts.
normal.cn: warmth 是名词；warmly 是热情的人做事的方式。

abstract.en: Picture two cupped hands around a mug: the word is a small, safe heat you can hold.
abstract.cn: 想象双手捧住一只杯子：这个词是可以握住的、安全的小小热度。

abstract.en: The same rise in temperature serves both skin and feeling, so friendliness is spoken of as heat.
abstract.cn: 同一种温度上升同时服务于皮肤与情感，于是友善被说成热度。

abstract.en: Warmth is always comparative in practice: warm relative to the air, the room, or the person.
abstract.cn: 温暖在实践中总是相对的：相对于空气、房间或那个人。

examples.en: The stone wall stayed warm long after sunset.
examples.cn: 日落很久之后，那面石墙还是暖的。

examples.en: She warmed her hands over the small stove.
examples.cn: 她把手放在小炉子上取暖。

examples.en: The villagers gave the teachers a warm welcome.
examples.cn: 村民们热情地欢迎这些老师。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我母」——我母亲的手总是暖的：温暖的

root: 古英语 wearm「暖的」，源自日耳曼语同一词根，与德语 warm、荷兰语 warm 同源；派生词有 warmth、warmly、warmer。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of warm share one moderate heat: pleasant air, clothing that keeps it, a friendly manner, the act of adding heat, and finally the slow warming of affection.
sensesIntro.cn: warm 的五个义项共用同一种适中的热：宜人的空气、留热的衣物、亲切的态度、加热的动作，最后是感情慢慢变暖。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands cupped around a mug of hot tea, fingers slowly coming back to life.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手捧住一杯热茶，指尖慢慢回温。

branches.en: AIR LINE: heat that feels good on the skin.
branches.cn: 空气线：皮肤上觉得舒服的热。

branches.en: CLOTHING LINE: heat held close to the body.
branches.cn: 衣物线：紧贴身体留住的热。

branches.en: FEELING LINE: friendliness, and its slow rising.
branches.cn: 情感线：亲切，以及它缓慢的升温。

branches.en: ACTION LINE: heat applied a little at a time.
branches.cn: 动作线：一点一点加上的热。

branches.en: CONTRAST: hot burns, warm comforts, lukewarm disappoints.
branches.cn: 对照线：hot 烫，warm 舒服，lukewarm 让人失望。

intro.en: Warm is a native Germanic word; the endings it takes are ordinary English suffixes.
intro.cn: warm 是本族日耳曼语词；它接的都是普通英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is involved here; the related native forms are listed instead.
latinIntro.cn: 此处不涉及拉丁语成分，只列出相关的本族词形式。

definition_zh: 警告；提醒；告诫；预先通知
definition_en: to tell someone about a possible danger or problem so that they can avoid it
core_image: 一个人伸手拦住同伴，指着前方，要他在踏出下一步之前先停下
scene: 山路边的牌子被风吹得咣咣响，护林员在岔口拦住游客。He warned us that the path would be icy after dark.
sceneCN: 这里 warn 是「警告、提醒」（第 1 个义项：告知可能发生的危险，以便对方避开）；句意为他提醒我们天黑后小路会结冰。伸手拦住同伴的动作，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 动词：警告、告诫；提醒；预先通知

collocations.zh: 受到警告；要有心理准备

derivatives.zh: 加 -ing 构成，义为「警告；警告信号」
由过去分词转形容词，义为「已受警告的」
加后缀 -er 构成，义为「警告者；报警装置」
加前缀 fore- 构成，义为「预先警告」

senses.title: To tell of danger
senses.definition: to tell someone about a danger or problem before it happens
senses.definitionCN: 在危险或问题发生之前告诉某人
senses.example: The coastguard warned the boats about the coming storm.
senses.exampleCN: 海岸警卫队警告船只将有暴风雨来袭。
senses.why: Old English warnian meant to take heed and to admonish; the word names the act of making someone careful before harm arrives.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 warnian 意为留心与告诫；这个词指在伤害到来之前使人警醒的动作。

senses.title: To advise against
senses.definition: to advise someone strongly not to do something
senses.definitionCN: 强烈劝告某人不要做某事
senses.example: Doctors warn against taking the pills on an empty stomach.
senses.exampleCN: 医生告诫不要空腹服用这些药片。
senses.why: The same forward look is aimed at an action: the danger is what the doing would bring, so the advice is a prohibition.
senses.whyCN: 同样是对未来的注视，只是这次落在某个动作上：危险正是这个动作会带来的，所以劝告成了禁令。

senses.title: To give notice in advance
senses.titleCN: 预先通知：提前告知某事会来
senses.definition: to inform someone in advance that something is going to happen
senses.definitionCN: 提前告知某人某事即将发生
senses.example: Nobody warned me that the office would close early.
senses.exampleCN: 没有人提前告诉我办公室会提前关门。
senses.why: With danger taken out, only the timing remains: the word still speaks of a thing before it happens.
senses.whyCN: 把危险抽掉之后，只剩下时间关系：这个词说的仍是事情发生之前的那一句话。

senses.title: To caution officially
senses.titleCN: 正式警告：由权威出面告诫
senses.definition: to caution a person officially, especially about behaviour or breaking a rule
senses.definitionCN: 由官方或权威出面告诫某人，尤指其行为或违规
senses.example: The referee warned the player before showing the card.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判在出示牌之前先警告了这名球员。
senses.why: An authority repeats the hedge at the cliff edge in a formal voice, and the next step is a penalty.
senses.whyCN: 权威以正式的口吻重演崖边那道拦阻，而下一步就是处罚。

senses.title: To keep someone off
senses.titleCN: 警告离开：阻止某人靠近
senses.definition: in the phrase warn off, to tell someone to stay away from a place or a person
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 warn off，令某人远离某地或某人
senses.example: The farmer warned the walkers off the closed field.
senses.exampleCN: 农场主警告散步的人离开那片封闭的田地。
senses.why: Here the warning becomes a wall of words: the message is not what to watch but where not to stand.
senses.whyCN: 此时警告变成了一道用话砌成的墙：信息不是该注意什么，而是不该站在哪里。

intro.en: Warn comes from an Old English word for refusing or forbidding, and it is close kin to 'beware'.
intro.cn: warn 来自古英语中表示「拒绝、禁止」的词，与 beware 关系很近。

items.en: Warnian meant 'to take heed, be careful', and also 'to admonish or forbid'.
items.cn: warnian 意为「留心、当心」，也表示「告诫、禁止」。

items.en: The noun waru meant 'care, protection, guard', part of the same Germanic cluster.
items.cn: 名词 waru 意为「注意、保护、看守」，属于同一日耳曼词群。

items.en: German warnen 'to warn' and Dutch waarschuwen in part share this history.
items.cn: 德语 warnen 与荷兰语的部分说法共享这段历史。

items.en: The shorter form warn came from the infinitive warnian, and the beware sense drifted to the separate word beware.
items.cn: 较短形式 warn 出自不定式 warnian，而「当心」这一义则漂移到独立词 beware 上。

items.en: The present range runs from a shout at a cliff edge to a formal letter from a court.
items.cn: 现代用法从崖边的呼喊一直到法庭的正式函件。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with the warn / war shape; the near-meaning group gathers ways of telling people about risk.
note.cn: 形近组收形状相近的 warn、war 类词；近义组收告知风险的多种说法。

entries.definition: A statement or sign that tells of danger.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「警告；警示」，指告知危险的话语或标志。

entries.definition: To be careful of something; the old be-wary sense kept as its own word.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「当心」，把古老的「警觉」义保存为独立词。

entries.definition: The past participle of wear, meaning used or damaged; a homophone trap.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，是 wear 的过去分词，意为磨损的；与本词同音，是易混点。

entries.definition: To twist out of shape; an unrelated word of different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「翘曲、扭曲」，与本词只是形近，来源无关。

entries.definition: To tell someone to be ready for danger; often brief and urgent.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使警觉」，多用于简短紧急的提醒。

entries.definition: To tell someone to be careful, often in a gentler or official tone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「告诫」，语气较轻或偏正式。

entries.definition: To state an intention to harm; the warning becomes hostile.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「威胁」，警告在此变成了敌意。

entries.definition: To give someone advice about what to do; warmer and less about danger.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「建议」，语气更和气，重点不在危险。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English warnian and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语 warnian，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: Warn, not scold: the point is to stop something before it hurts.
normal.cn: warn 不是责骂：要点是在造成伤害之前拦住它。

normal.en: Warn of a thing, warn against an action: the preposition shows the target.
normal.cn: warn of 后接事物，warn against 后接动作：介词显示对象。

normal.en: Beware carries the old careful sense of warn away as its own word.
normal.cn: beware 把 warn 古老的「当心」义带走，成了独立词。

normal.en: A warning can be a word, a sign or a red light.
normal.cn: warning 可以是一句话、一块标志牌或一盏红灯。

normal.en: Worn is a homophone and means used up: do not mix the two.
normal.cn: worn 是同音词，意为磨旧的：不要混用。

abstract.en: Picture a hand on a companion's chest at the edge of a cliff: the body stops first, the explanation comes after.
abstract.cn: 想象在崖边一只手按住同伴的胸口：身体先停下，解释随后才来。

abstract.en: The word faces forward in time: it only works if heard before the harm.
abstract.cn: 这个词朝向未来：只有在伤害之前被听见，它才起作用。

abstract.en: From a shout to a printed notice to a court letter, the same forward-looking alarm.
abstract.cn: 从一声呼喊到一张通告，再到一封法庭来函，是同一种前瞻性的警报。

examples.en: The guide warned us that the bridge might be unsafe.
examples.cn: 导游提醒我们那座桥可能不安全。

examples.en: Doctors warn against skipping breakfast every day.
examples.cn: 医生告诫不要每天都不吃早饭。

examples.en: A red light warns drivers when the crossing is busy.
examples.cn: 人行横道忙碌时，红灯会提醒司机。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「网」——路边拉了红色警示网，提醒你别再往前走：警告

root: 古英语 warnian「留心、告诫、禁止」，与 waru「注意、保护」同属一个日耳曼词群；beware 保存了其中「当心」的一支；派生词有 warning、forewarn。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of warn all face forward in time: danger ahead, an action to avoid, news in advance, official caution, and a call to keep away.
sensesIntro.cn: warn 的五个义项都朝向未来：前方的危险、要避开的动作、提前的通告、正式的告诫，以及令人远离的喝止。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand held out against a companion's chest at the edge of a cliff.
core.cn: 核心意象：崖边一只横在同伴胸前的手。

branches.en: DANGER LINE: the word points at what is coming.
branches.cn: 危险线：这个词指着即将到来的东西。

branches.en: ACTION LINE: the advice is aimed at what not to do.
branches.cn: 动作线：劝告落在不该做的事上。

branches.en: NOTICE LINE: the warning may be plain information in advance.
branches.cn: 通知线：警告也可能只是提前告知信息。

branches.en: AUTHORITY LINE: an official voice repeats the same caution.
branches.cn: 权威线：官方声音重复同样的告诫。

branches.en: DISTANCE LINE: warn off pushes the person away.
branches.cn: 距离线：warn off 把人推得更远。

intro.en: Warn is a native verb; its relatives in English are the endings it takes and the beware branch.
intro.cn: warn 是本族动词；它在英语中的亲属是所接的词尾以及 beware 这一分支。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is involved here; the related native forms are listed instead.
latinIntro.cn: 此处不涉及拉丁语成分，只列出相关的本族词形式。

items.example: It belongs to the same cluster.
items.exampleCN: 它与本词同属一个词群。

definition_zh: 洗；洗涤；冲洗；（水）冲刷；名词：洗；待洗的衣物
definition_en: to clean something with water and usually soap, or the act of cleaning this way
core_image: 一盆水被搅动，脏东西被水带走，露出底下干净的一层
scene: 傍晚的院子里，母亲把沾满泥的孩子的手按进盆里来回搓。Wash your hands before you sit down at the table.
sceneCN: 这里 wash 是「洗、洗涤」（第 1 个义项：用水和肥皂把东西弄干净）；句意为坐到桌前先把手洗干净。把脏东西用水带走，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：洗；洗过的衣物；（水的）冲刷

derivatives.zh: 加 -ing 构成，义为「洗涤；待洗的衣物」
加后缀 -er 构成，义为「洗衣机；垫圈」
加后缀 -able 构成，义为「可水洗的」

senses.title: To clean with water
senses.definition: to clean something with water, usually with soap
senses.definitionCN: 用水清洗某物，通常加肥皂
senses.example: She washed the dusty cups under the tap.
senses.exampleCN: 她在水龙头下把积尘的杯子洗了。
senses.why: Old English wascan meant to wash, and the whole family in northern Europe carries the same simple action.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 wascan 意为「洗」，北欧各语言的同源词都指向这一简单动作。

senses.title: To clean a body part
senses.titleCN: 洗（身体某部位）：把身上的脏东西去掉
senses.definition: to clean a part of the body, especially the hands or face
senses.definitionCN: 清洗身体的某一部分，尤指手和脸
senses.example: He washed his face in the cold stream.
senses.exampleCN: 他在冰冷的溪水里洗了脸。
senses.why: The object here is one's own body, so the verb often appears without a separate thing being washed.
senses.whyCN: 这里的对象是自己的身子，所以动词常不另带被洗的东西。

senses.title: To carry away by water
senses.definition: of water, to carry something away or to flow against a shore
senses.definitionCN: 指水流把东西带走，或拍打冲刷岸边
senses.example: The flood washed the bridge away in one night.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水一夜之间把桥冲走了。
senses.why: The same verb without soap: water still removes what it touches, only now nothing is cleaned.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词，不加肥皂：水依然带走它碰到的东西，只是这次什么都没被洗净。

senses.title: The act of washing
senses.definition: the act or occasion of cleaning with water
senses.definitionCN: 用水清洗的一次行为或场合
senses.example: The curtains could use a good wash.
senses.exampleCN: 这些窗帘该好好洗一次了。
senses.why: The verb turns into a countable noun, so the cleaning becomes something you can give a thing.
senses.whyCN: 动词转为名词，可以计数，于是清洗变成能给某物的一次处理。

senses.title: Clothes to be washed
senses.titleCN: 待洗的衣物：一堆要洗的东西
senses.definition: in the phrase the wash, the clothes and other items waiting to be or just cleaned
senses.definitionCN: 用于 the wash 这一说法，指待洗或刚洗好的衣物
senses.example: Her wet socks were still in the wash.
senses.exampleCN: 她湿掉的袜子还泡在待洗的衣物里。
senses.why: A concrete pile grows out of the abstract act: what is being washed becomes the wash itself.
senses.whyCN: 具体的一堆东西从抽象动作里长出来：正在被洗的东西本身就叫 the wash。

intro.en: Wash is an Old English verb, and nearly every Germanic language has a cousin of it.
intro.cn: wash 是古英语动词，几乎每种日耳曼语都有它的近亲。

items.en: Wascan meant 'to wash, to cleanse with water'; the noun wæsc meant a washing.
items.cn: wascan 意为「用水洗、洗净」，名词 wæsc 指一次洗涤。

items.en: German waschen and Dutch wassen are exact cognates of the same root.
items.cn: 德语 waschen 与荷兰语 wassen 是同一词根的精确同源词。

items.en: The root is related to words for water in older European languages; the exact reconstruction is debated.
items.cn: 这个词根与更古老欧洲语言中的「水」类词有关，确切重构仍有争议。

items.en: Wasshen kept both the cleaning sense and the sense of water sweeping things along.
items.cn: 中古英语 wasshen 既保留洗涤义，也保留水流冲走东西之义。

items.en: Machines gave the word new nouns: the washing, the washer, the wash cycle.
items.cn: 机器给了这个词新的名词：the washing、the washer、wash cycle。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with the wash shape; the near-meaning group gathers ways of cleaning.
note.cn: 形近组收形状相近的 wash 类词；近义组收各种清洁的说法。

entries.definition: The activity of washing, or the clothes being washed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「洗涤」或「待洗的衣物」。

entries.definition: A washing machine, or the flat ring that seals a joint.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「洗衣机」，或指密封用的垫圈。

entries.definition: Able to be washed without damage.
To look at steadily; a different word, close in sound only.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「观看」，只是发音相近，来源不同。

entries.definition: To clean with clean water only, without soap.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「冲洗」，只用水不用肥皂。

entries.definition: To remove dirt in any way; broader than wash.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「清洁」，方式不限，范围比 wash 宽。

entries.definition: To wash a whole body in a bath or the sea.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「沐浴」，指整体泡洗。

entries.definition: To rub hard with a brush; more force than wash.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「刷洗」，比 wash 用力得多。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English wascan and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语 wascan，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: Water plus friction: that is the whole of wash.
normal.cn: 水加上摩擦：wash 的全部含义就在这里。

normal.en: Wash your hands, wash the dishes, wash the car: the object changes, the action does not.
normal.cn: 洗手、洗碗、洗车：对象在变，动作不变。

normal.en: Wash away means the water takes it off; wash off means you remove it.
normal.cn: wash away 是水把它带走，wash off 是你把它去掉。

normal.en: The wash is not the act but the pile of clothes waiting.
normal.cn: the wash 不是动作，而是等着洗的那堆衣服。

normal.en: Washing machine, dish washer, washroom: machines borrowed the old verb.
normal.cn: washing machine、dish washer、washroom：机器借用了这个古老动词。

abstract.en: Picture dirt loosened by water and carried off: the word always has something leaving.
abstract.cn: 想象脏东西被水泡松、被带走：这个词永远有个东西正在离开。

abstract.en: The same verb serves skin, dishes, clothes and even bridges, because water behaves the same way everywhere.
abstract.cn: 同一个动词适用于皮肤、碗碟、衣物甚至桥梁，因为水在各处都一样作为。

abstract.en: Cleaning and carrying away are one motion seen from two ends: what leaves the cup is what cleans it.
abstract.cn: 清洁与带走是同一动作的两端：离开杯子的东西正是清洗它的东西。

examples.en: Wash the vegetables under cold running water.
examples.cn: 在冷流水下冲洗蔬菜。

examples.en: The storm washed the soil off the hillside.
examples.cn: 暴雨把山坡上的泥土冲走了。

examples.en: There is a big wash waiting on Sunday morning.
examples.cn: 星期天早上有一大堆衣服等着洗。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我洗」——wash 听起来就像「我洗」：洗

root: 古英语 wascan「洗、洗净」，源自日耳曼语同一词根，与德语 waschen、荷兰语 wassen 同源；派生词有 washing、washer、washable。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of wash follow water at work: cleaning a thing, cleaning the body, carrying something away, the act itself, and finally the pile of clothes.
sensesIntro.cn: wash 的五个义项跟着水在工作：洗净物件、清洗身体、把东西带走、动作本身，最后是那堆衣服。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a basin of water stirred, dirt lifted off, a clean surface underneath.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盆水被搅动，脏物离开，露出底下干净的一层。

branches.en: CLEANING LINE: objects and bodies come out clean.
branches.cn: 清洁线：物件与身体被洗得干净。

branches.en: FORCE LINE: water without soap simply takes things away.
branches.cn: 冲力线：没有肥皂的水只是把东西带走。

branches.en: ACT LINE: one wash counted as one occasion.
branches.cn: 动作线：一次洗算作一次。

branches.en: OBJECT LINE: the clothes themselves become the wash.
branches.cn: 物件线：衣服本身成了 the wash。

branches.en: CONTRAST: rinse is water only, scrub is force, clean is any way.
branches.cn: 对照线：rinse 只用水，scrub 靠力，clean 方式不限。

intro.en: Wash is a native verb, and its derivatives are built with ordinary English endings.
intro.cn: wash 是本族动词，其派生词都由普通英语词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is involved here; the related native forms are listed instead.
latinIntro.cn: 此处不涉及拉丁语成分，只列出相关的本族词形式。

definition_zh: 浪费；废物、垃圾；浪费的时间或金钱；动词：浪费、滥用；荒废的
definition_en: to use something carelessly so that it is lost, or material that is thrown away because it is no longer wanted
core_image: 水从没关紧的龙头里一直滴，地上积成一片没人要的湿痕
scene: 食堂收餐口的桶里堆着大半个没吃完的饭盒。So much food is wasted every day that the kitchen began weighing it.
sceneCN: 这里 waste 是「浪费」（第 4 个义项：不加珍惜地用掉，使之白白失去）；句意为每天浪费的食物太多，厨房开始称重。水白白流走、饭被倒掉，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：废物、垃圾；浪费；荒地

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -ful 构成，义为「浪费的；不节俭的」
加后缀 -age 构成，义为「损耗；浪费量」
加后缀 -er 构成，义为「浪费者；废品」
由过去分词转形容词，义为「被浪费的；憔悴的」

senses.title: A desert or empty land
senses.titleCN: 荒地：无人居住的空旷之地
senses.definition: a large area of land that is empty, wild and not used for farming
senses.definitionCN: 大片空旷、野生、不用于耕种的土地
senses.example: Beyond the last field lies a wide waste of stone and thorn.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一块田之外，是一片石头与荆棘的荒地。
senses.why: Old French wast meant empty and desolate, and English kept that picture of land with nothing on it.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 wast 意为「空的、荒凉的」，英语保留了那片空无一物的土地的画面。

senses.title: To destroy and leave empty
senses.titleCN: 使荒芜：毁坏而使之空无
senses.definition: to damage a place so badly that it is left empty or ruined
senses.definitionCN: 把某地毁坏到空无或残破的地步
senses.example: The long war wasted the whole valley.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长的战争让整个山谷变得荒芜。
senses.why: The adjective of emptiness becomes an action: to make a place into a waste.
senses.whyCN: 表示「空」的形容词变成动作：把某地变成一片荒地。

senses.title: Rubbish and unwanted material
senses.titleCN: 废物、垃圾：不再需要而被丢弃的东西
senses.definition: material that is no longer wanted and is thrown away
senses.definitionCN: 已不需要、被丢弃的物质
senses.example: The factory must treat its waste before it enters the river.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂必须先把废物处理掉，才能排入河中。
senses.why: What is left after use is like a wasteland: nothing grows on it, so it is set aside.
senses.whyCN: 用剩下的东西就像荒地：上面长不出什么，只好被弃置一旁。

senses.title: To use carelessly
senses.definition: to use money, time or effort badly, so that it brings no benefit
senses.definitionCN: 不善加利用金钱、时间或精力，使之无所收益
senses.example: Do not waste hot water on a small load of dishes.
senses.exampleCN: 别为几个碗浪费热水。
senses.why: Spending what could have been used well turns a resource into waste; the verb names that turning.
senses.whyCN: 把本可好好利用的东西花掉，资源就变成了废物；动词命名的正是这一转变。

senses.title: As in wasted effort or a wasted chance
senses.titleCN: 白白错过：努力或机会被耗掉
senses.definition: used of effort, opportunity or a person's condition when something valuable comes to nothing
senses.definitionCN: 用于努力、机会或人的状态，指宝贵的东西最终落空
senses.example: All their careful planning was wasted when the road was closed.
senses.exampleCN: 路一封闭，他们所有的精心安排都白费了。
senses.why: The lost value is no longer money but possibility: what might have happened now cannot.
senses.whyCN: 失去的不再是钱，而是可能性：本可能发生的事如今不可能了。

intro.en: Waste came from Latin vastus through Old French, and its first meaning was empty land.
intro.cn: waste 经古法语来自拉丁语 vastus，最初的意思是空旷的土地。

items.en: Vastus meant 'empty, desolate, huge'; the emptiness came before the size in English use.
items.cn: vastus 意为「空的、荒凉的、巨大的」；在英语用法中，空义先于大义。

items.en: The verb vastare meant 'to lay waste, to devastate', turning emptiness into an action.
items.cn: 动词 vastare 意为「使荒芜、毁坏」，把「空」变成了动作。

items.en: Old French had both gast and waste, meaning 'empty, ruined' and 'a waste place'.
items.cn: 古法语有 gast 与 waste 两种形式，意为「空的、毁坏的」与「荒地」。

items.en: English took waste as noun, adjective and verb together in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪同时把 waste 用作名词、形容词和动词。

items.en: Industry added the rubbish sense: household waste, waste paper, waste water.
items.cn: 工业补充了垃圾义：生活垃圾、废纸、废水。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same empty-root family; the near-meaning group gathers ways of squandering and of rubbish.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「空」词根词族；近义组收挥霍与垃圾类说法。

entries.definition: Extremely large; the same Latin vastus, with the size sense only.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「辽阔的」，同出拉丁语 vastus，只保留「大」义。

entries.definition: To destroy a place completely; Latin de- plus vastare.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「毁坏」，由 de- 加 vastare 构成。

entries.definition: Using more than is needed; the adjective of the squandering sense.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「浪费的」，是挥霍义的形容词形式。

entries.definition: Land that is empty and cannot be farmed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「荒地」，即空旷无法耕种之地。

entries.definition: To spend money or time foolishly; stronger and more disapproving.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「挥霍」，语气更强、更带责备。

entries.definition: Unwanted things; the British everyday word for waste.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「垃圾」，是英式日常说法。

entries.definition: Waste food and household rubbish; the American everyday word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「垃圾」，尤指厨余，是美式日常说法。

entries.definition: To give or use without harming oneself; the opposite of wasting.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「腾出、剩下」，与浪费相对。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin vastus and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语 vastus，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: waste and vast share a root: empty land, and land just very big.
normal.cn: waste 与 vast 同根：一片是空地，一片只是很大。

normal.en: To waste is to turn a resource into rubbish.
normal.cn: waste 就是把资源变成垃圾。

normal.en: A waste of time costs more than a waste of paper.
normal.cn: 浪费时间的代价比浪费纸张大得多。

normal.en: Household waste is what leaves the house to be thrown away.
normal.cn: household waste 就是被运出家门的垃圾。

normal.en: Lay waste to a place and it becomes a waste: the verb and the noun meet.
normal.cn: lay waste to 一个地方，它就变成一片 waste：动词与名词在此相遇。

abstract.en: Picture a tap left dripping overnight: the water is not dirty, only lost.
abstract.cn: 想象一只水龙头一夜没关紧：水并不脏，只是白白流掉了。

abstract.en: The two halves of the word meet at the same point: what is thrown away is what was never used well.
abstract.cn: 这个词的两半在同一点相遇：被丢弃的，正是从未被好好利用的。

abstract.en: Emptiness is the hinge: a wasted field, a wasted chance and a waste bin all hold nothing useful.
abstract.cn: 空是那个铰链：荒掉的地、白费的机会、垃圾箱，都装着没用的东西。

examples.en: He wasted two hours waiting for a bus that never came.
examples.cn: 他白等了两个小时，那趟公交始终没来。

examples.en: The city collects household waste every Tuesday.
examples.cn: 这座城市每周二收集生活垃圾。

examples.en: It is a waste of money to buy a new one when this still works.
examples.cn: 这个还能用，再买个新的纯属浪费钱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂（wei）死它（ste）」——把好东西喂给垃圾桶，活活浪费：浪费

root: 源自拉丁语 vastus「空的、荒凉的」，动词 vastare「使荒芜」，经古法语 waste 进入英语；同族词有 vast、devastate。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of waste start from empty land, move to the act of emptying a place, then to rubbish, to squandering, and finally to any chance that comes to nothing.
sensesIntro.cn: waste 的五个义项从荒地开始，到把地方弄空的动作，再到垃圾、挥霍，最后是一切落空的机会。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tap left dripping overnight, the water lost without ever being dirty.
core.cn: 核心意象：一夜没关紧的水龙头，水并不脏，却全部流失。

branches.en: LAND LINE: empty ground, and the act of making it empty.
branches.cn: 土地线：空旷的地，以及把它弄空的动作。

branches.en: RUBBISH LINE: what use leaves behind is thrown away.
branches.cn: 垃圾线：使用之后剩下的被丢弃。

branches.en: SQUANDER LINE: resources used so badly they become rubbish.
branches.cn: 挥霍线：资源被用得极糟，于是成了垃圾。

branches.en: CHANCE LINE: the lost thing is now possibility, not money.
branches.cn: 机会线：失去的已是可能性而非金钱。

branches.en: CONTRAST: spare keeps something; waste loses it.
branches.cn: 对照线：spare 留下东西，waste 让它失去。

intro.en: Waste is a Latin adjective and verb that English turned into three word classes at once.
intro.cn: waste 本是拉丁语的形容词与动词，英语把它一次性用成了三种词类。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is documented: vastus and vastare.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础有据可查：vastus 与 vastare。

definition_zh: 观看；注视；看护；手表；看守；值班
definition_en: to look at something attentively over a period of time, and a small clock worn on the wrist
core_image: 一个人停在路边，眼睛跟着走过的东西慢慢转动
scene: 球场边有人站着不动，眼睛始终追着那只球。He kept watch at the gate until dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 watch 是「观看、注视」（第 1 个义项：持续一段时间专注地看）；句意为他在门口守夜到天亮。眼睛跟着球慢慢转动的那幅画就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 加 -er 构成，义为「观察者；看守人」
加 -ful 构成，义为「警惕的；留心的」
复合词，义为「守夜人；更夫」

senses.title: To look at for a while
senses.definition: to look at someone or something attentively for a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间内专注地看某人或某物
senses.example: They watched the boats come in from the harbour wall.
senses.exampleCN: 他们站在港口的堤上看船进港。
senses.why: The oldest sense is steady looking, which is the base for all the others.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是持续地看，这是其余义项的基础。

senses.title: To guard or look after
senses.definition: to stay with someone or something in order to protect or care for it
senses.definitionCN: 守着某人或某物以保护或照看
senses.example: A nurse watched the child through the night.
senses.exampleCN: 一位护士整夜照看那个孩子。
senses.why: A watcher who stays awake to protect is doing the same thing as watching, only with a duty attached.
senses.whyCN: 醒着守候以保护别人的人，做的仍是「看」，只是多了一份职责。

senses.title: To be careful of
senses.definition: to be careful about something, especially in the phrase watch out
senses.definitionCN: 对某事小心，尤用于 watch out 这一说法
senses.example: Watch out for the step at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 当心门口的台阶。
senses.why: To be careful is to keep your eyes on a danger, so the verb of looking came to mean warning.
senses.whyCN: 小心就是盯着危险看，于是表示「看」的动词也有了提醒之意。

senses.title: The clock on the wrist
senses.definition: a small clock worn on the wrist or carried in a pocket
senses.definitionCN: 戴在腕上或装在口袋里的小钟表
senses.example: His watch stopped at ten past four.
senses.exampleCN: 他的手表停在四点十分。
senses.why: Early watches were carried by men who had to stay awake on duty, and the little clock took the name of that duty.
senses.whyCN: 早期的表由必须保持清醒值守的人携带，这只小钟便沿用了「值守」这个名字。

senses.title: A period of duty
senses.definition: a period of time during which a person is on duty, especially on a ship
senses.definitionCN: 某人值班的一段时间，尤指在船上
senses.example: The captain took the first watch of the night.
senses.exampleCN: 船长值了夜里的第一班岗。
senses.why: Sailors divided the night into named watches, and the word still means the stretch of duty itself.
senses.whyCN: 水手把夜晚分成若干有名目的班次，这个词至今仍指那一段值守时间。

intro.en: Watch began as a verb meaning to stay awake, and only later came to mean to look and then the little clock itself.
intro.cn: watch 起初是「保持清醒」的动词，后来才指「看」，最后又指那只小钟。

items.en: The verb wæccan meant to be awake or to keep awake, often at night.
items.cn: 动词 wæccan 意为「醒着」或「使人不睡」，常在夜里使用。

items.en: A related noun wæcc gave watch in the sense of a period of staying awake.
items.cn: 同源名词 wæcc 衍生出「守夜时段」这一义的 watch。

items.en: By the fourteenth century watch meant both to be on guard and to look at, and the looking sense grew strong.
items.cn: 到十四世纪，watch 兼指「警戒」与「看」，而「看」这一义日益增强。

items.en: In the sixteenth century a small portable clock was called a watch, since it kept you awake on time.
items.cn: 十六世纪，小的便携钟表被称为 watch，因为它能按时把人叫醒。

items.en: The modern verb is used for television, games and any long, steady looking.
items.cn: 现代用法中，这个动词覆盖电视、比赛以及任何长时间持续的看。

note.en: The first group gathers forms and look-alikes of watch, the second the verbs of looking and the other timepiece words.
note.cn: 第一组收 watch 的形式与形近词，第二组收「看」一类动词以及钟表词。

entries.definition: Third person singular and the plural of the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 第三人称单数，也是名词复数

One who watches.

entries.definition: To protect by staying near.

normalIntro.en: Awake, then look, then a small clock: the history runs from staying alert to telling the time.
normalIntro.cn: 先醒着，再看，最后是只小钟：历史从「保持警觉」走到「报时」。

normal.en: Watch out is a warning: keep your eyes on the danger.
normal.cn: watch out 是提醒：眼睛盯着危险。

normal.en: You watch TV but you look at a picture.
normal.cn: watch TV 只看电视，看一幅画用 look at。

normal.en: Keep watch is to stay awake and guard.
normal.cn: keep watch 是守夜警戒。

normal.en: A watch on the wrist, a clock on the wall.
normal.cn: 腕上是 watch，墙上是 clock。

normal.en: Add -ful for the adjective: watchful, alert.
normal.cn: 加 -ful 得形容词：watchful（警觉的）。

abstract.en: See a still figure whose eyes follow a passing boat.
abstract.cn: 想一个不动的人，眼睛跟着经过的船。

abstract.en: Feel a night spent awake by a door.
abstract.cn: 感受在门边醒着度过的一夜。

abstract.en: Picture a small dial ticking on a wrist.
abstract.cn: 想腕上一只小表盘在走。

examples.en: We watched the sun go down behind the hills.
examples.cn: 我们看着太阳落到山后。

examples.en: Could you watch my bag for a minute?
examples.cn: 你能帮我看一下包吗？

examples.en: Watch out for ice on the path.
examples.cn: 当心小路上的冰。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瓦奇」——瓦奇守在门口一动不动，眼睛一直盯着走廊尽头，连表都忘了看。

root: 古英语 wæccan（保持清醒、守夜）与同源名词 wæcc（守夜时段）合为 watch。

sensesIntro.en: Steady looking comes first, then guarding, then the warning, and finally the wrist clock and the night watch on a ship.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是持续地看，接着是守护，然后是提醒，最后落在腕上的表与船上的夜班岗。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an eye following a moving thing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只跟着移动之物转动的眼睛。

branches.en: The looking branch: boats coming into harbour.
branches.cn: 观看分支：进港的船。

branches.en: The guarding branch: a nurse through the night.
branches.cn: 守护分支：守夜的护士。

branches.en: The warning branch: a step at the door.
branches.cn: 提醒分支：门口的台阶。

branches.en: The timepiece branch: a dial that stopped.
branches.cn: 钟表分支：停住的小表盘。

branches.en: The duty branch: the captain’s first watch.
branches.cn: 值班分支：船长的第一班岗。

intro.en: Watch takes -er for the person, -ful for the adjective and -es in the third person, and combines in watchman and stopwatch.
intro.cn: watch 加 -er 成指人的词，加 -ful 成形容词，第三人称加 -es，还与 man、stop 组成复合词。

latinIntro.en: Watch is native English from Old English wæccan, with no Latin source, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: watch 是源自古英语 wæccan 的本族词，没有拉丁语来源，故拉丁条目为空。

items.example: The stem of the whole family.

definition_zh: 水；水域；浇水；给…喝水
definition_en: the clear liquid that falls as rain and fills rivers and seas, and to pour it on plants or give it to animals
core_image: 一捧从井里舀起的水，指缝间淌下细细的水线
scene: 她每天清早提着桶去井边，回来时鞋上全湿了。The garden needs to be watered twice a week in summer.
sceneCN: 这里 water 是「水」（第 1 个义项：雨水、河海中那种清澈的液体）；句意为夏天花园需要每周浇两次水。从指缝间淌下的水线就是这个词给的画面。

derivatives.zh: 加 -y 构成，义为「含水的；稀薄的」
加 -ing 构成，义为「浇水；灌溉」

senses.title: The liquid we drink
senses.definition: the clear liquid that has no colour, taste or smell, and that all life needs
senses.definitionCN: 无色无味、一切生命都需要的清澈液体
senses.example: He drank a glass of water and sat down.
senses.exampleCN: 他喝了一杯水，然后坐下。
senses.why: The basic sense is the liquid itself, the one thing the word has meant for over a thousand years.
senses.whyCN: 基本义就是这种液体本身，一千多年来这个词一直指它。

senses.title: A sea, lake or river area
senses.definition: in the plural or with a modifier, an area of sea, lake or river
senses.definitionCN: 用复数或加修饰语，指海、湖或河的一片区域
senses.example: The boat drifted into shallow waters near the shore.
senses.exampleCN: 小船漂进了近岸的浅水区。
senses.why: Where the liquid lies in a body large enough to name, the plural waters marks out that area.
senses.whyCN: 当这种液体聚成足够大、值得命名的一片时，用复数 waters 指那片区域。

senses.title: To pour water on plants
senses.definition: to pour water on plants or soil so that they can grow
senses.definitionCN: 给植物或土壤浇水以助其生长
senses.example: She waters the herbs every morning before work.
senses.exampleCN: 她每天上班前给香草浇水。
senses.why: Making the noun do the work of a verb is the simplest step: to water is to give water.
senses.whyCN: 让名词直接充当动词是最简单的一步：water 就是给水。

senses.title: Of the eyes, to fill with tears
senses.definition: of the eyes, to fill with tears, often because of wind or onions
senses.definitionCN: 眼睛因风或洋葱等而充满泪水
senses.example: The smoke made his eyes water.
senses.exampleCN: 烟熏得他眼睛流泪。
senses.why: The eye filling with liquid is water appearing where it does not belong, so the verb describes that too.
senses.whyCN: 眼里盈满液体，就是水出现在了不该出现的地方，于是动词也兼指此事。

senses.title: To give animals a drink
senses.definition: to lead animals to drink or to give them water
senses.definitionCN: 把牲畜牵去饮水或给它们水喝
senses.example: He watered the horses before the long ride.
senses.exampleCN: 长途骑行之前他先给马饮了水。
senses.why: Farm work made this a fixed use early: to water stock is to supply the one thing they must have.
senses.whyCN: 农活很早就固定了这一用法：water 牲畜就是供给它们必不可少的那个东西。

intro.en: Water is one of the oldest words in English, with the same root in German Wasser and Dutch water.
intro.cn: water 是英语最古老的词之一，德语 Wasser 与荷兰语 water 都出自同一词根。

items.en: The word was wæter, and it already meant both the liquid and a body of it.
items.cn: 古英语中作 wæter，当时就已兼指这种液体和一片水域。

items.en: The Germanic stem wat- spread across the family, giving German Wasser and Dutch water.
items.cn: 日耳曼词干 wat- 遍布整个语族，产生德语 Wasser 与荷兰语 water。

items.en: The root behind it probably meant wet or flow, linking the word to the way the liquid moves.
items.cn: 其词根大概意为「湿的、流动的」，把词与这种液体的流动方式联系起来。

items.en: The form water established itself and the verb to water appeared beside the noun.
items.cn: water 这一形式确立，动词 to water 也随名词出现。

items.en: The word then joined in dozens of compounds, from waterfall to waterproof, and in idioms for trouble.
items.cn: 此后这个词参与了大量复合词（从 waterfall 到 waterproof），也进入表示困境的习语。

note.en: The first group gathers compounds and forms of water, the second the words for the liquid in other states and for nearby things.
note.cn: 第一组收 water 的复合词与词形，第二组收液体的其他状态词与相关词。

entries.definition: Third person singular and the plural noun.
entries.definitionCN: 第三人称单数，也是名词复数

entries.definition: Past tense and past participle.
The adjective meaning full of water.
The -ing form and the noun for the job.
entries.definitionCN: 现在分词，也是表示浇水这一工作的名词

entries.definition: Anything that flows, water included.
Water made solid by cold.
Water turned to gas by heat.
Water falling from the clouds.

normalIntro.en: One old word for the liquid serves both as noun and as verb, and builds compounds by the dozen.
normalIntro.cn: 这个古老的液体名词既作名词也作动词，还能造出大量复合词。

normal.en: Water the plants: the noun is the verb.
normal.cn: water the plants：名词直接作动词。

normal.en: Waters means a stretch of sea or lake, not several liquids.
normal.cn: waters 指一片海或湖，而不是几种液体。

normal.en: In deep water means in trouble.
normal.cn: in deep water 意为陷入困境。

normal.en: Waterproof is water plus proof, able to keep it out.
normal.cn: waterproof 是 water 加 proof：能挡住水。

normal.en: Water becomes ice and steam: liquid, solid, gas.
normal.cn: 水可成冰也可成汽：液态、固态、气态。

abstract.en: Picture water slipping between your fingers.
abstract.cn: 想水从指缝间滑下。

abstract.en: Hear a hose spitting over flower beds.
abstract.cn: 听水管在花坛上洒水的声音。

abstract.en: Feel cold water up to the knees.
abstract.cn: 感受没到膝盖的冷水。

examples.en: The lake water was still and very cold.
examples.cn: 湖水静止，冰凉得很。

examples.en: Someone should water these flowers.
examples.cn: 得有人来浇一浇这些花。

examples.en: The company is in deep water over the deal.
examples.cn: 这家公司因这桩交易陷入困境。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「沃特」——沃特每天提着桶把菜地浇得湿漉漉的，桶沿还一路滴着水。

root: 古英语 wæter，来自日耳曼词干 wat-（湿的、流动），与德语 Wasser 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The liquid comes first, then a stretch of it, then the verb of pouring and drinking, and finally the tear in the eye.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是这种液体，接着是一片水域，然后是浇水与饮水的动作，最后是眼中的泪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water running through open fingers.
core.cn: 核心意象：从张开的指缝间流过的水。

branches.en: The liquid branch: a glass after a meal.
branches.cn: 液体分支：饭后的一杯水。

branches.en: The waters branch: a boat in shallow waters.
branches.cn: 水域分支：浅水中的小船。

branches.en: The pouring branch: herbs watered at dawn.
branches.cn: 浇灌分支：清早浇过的香草。

branches.en: The eye branch: smoke that makes eyes water.
branches.cn: 眼睛分支：熏得流泪的烟。

branches.en: The stock branch: horses watered before the ride.
branches.cn: 牲畜分支：出发前饮过水的马。

intro.en: Water takes -y and -ing, -ed and -es, and serves as the first element of many compounds such as waterproof and underwater.
intro.cn: water 可加 -y、-ing、-ed、-es，并作为前项构成 waterproof、underwater 等大量复合词。

latinIntro.en: Water is one of the oldest Germanic words in English and has no Latin source, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: water 是英语中最古老的日耳曼词之一，没有拉丁语来源，故拉丁条目为空。

definition_zh: 波浪；挥手；挥动；（情绪的）浪潮；（头发的）卷曲
definition_en: a raised line of water moving across the sea, a movement of the hand in greeting, and to move to and fro
core_image: 海面上一条隆起的浪线推过来，到岸边碎成一排白沫
scene: 船开出港后，甲板上的人一直朝岸上挥手，直到彼此只剩一个小点。A huge wave broke over the rocks.
sceneCN: 这里 wave 是「挥手」（第 2 个义项：抬手来回摆动作招呼）；句意为一个巨浪打过礁石。海面上那条隆起的浪线就是这个词给人的画面。

pos.zh: 波浪；挥手；浪潮；（头发的）卷曲

collocations.phrase: the wave broke on the shore

derivatives.zh: 加 -y 构成，义为「波浪形的；起伏的」
现在分词作形容词，义为「飘扬的；挥动的」
另加 -er 构成，义为「犹豫；摇摆」
复合词，义为「微波；微波炉」

senses.title: A line of water moving in
senses.definition: one of the ridges of water that move across the surface of the sea
senses.definitionCN: 海面上向前推进的一道道隆起的水脊
senses.example: A huge wave broke over the rocks.
senses.exampleCN: 一个巨浪打过礁石。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the moving ridge of water, whose rising and falling shape explains every other use.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是移动的水脊，它一起一伏的形状解释了其余所有用法。

senses.title: A movement of the hand
senses.definition: a movement of the hand from side to side, usually to greet or to say goodbye
senses.definitionCN: 手来回摆动的动作，通常用于招呼或告别
senses.example: She gave a quick wave from the window.
senses.exampleCN: 她在窗口很快地挥了下手。
senses.why: A hand moved to and fro draws the same shape as a wave of water, so the greeting took the sea word.
senses.whyCN: 手来回摆动画出的形状与海浪相同，于是招呼的动作借用了海的名字。

senses.title: To move the hand in greeting
senses.definition: to move the hand or an object to and fro, especially as a sign
senses.definitionCN: 使手或物体来回摆动，尤作示意
senses.example: He waved until the bus turned the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 他挥手直到公交车转过街角。
senses.why: The verb is the action behind the noun: what a wave in hand is doing is waving.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是名词背后的动作：手里那一下「浪」正在做的事就是挥。

senses.title: A rush of feeling or events
senses.definition: a sudden increase of an emotion, an activity or a group of things arriving together
senses.definitionCN: 情绪、活动或成群事物的突然涌现
senses.example: A wave of relief went through the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵宽慰掠过人群。
senses.why: A wave comes over you and then passes, which is exactly how a fit of feeling or a sudden arrival behaves.
senses.whyCN: 浪会扑上来又退下去，这与一阵情绪或一波涌来的事物正相像。

senses.title: Energy travelling through space
senses.definition: in physics, a disturbance that carries energy through a medium or through space
senses.definitionCN: 物理学中携带能量在介质或空间中传播的扰动
senses.example: Sound waves travel more slowly through water than through air.
senses.exampleCN: 声波在水中的传播比在空气中慢。
senses.why: Such a disturbance rises and falls in a regular pattern, so physics borrowed the sea word for it.
senses.whyCN: 这种扰动有规律地起伏，于是物理学借用了海的词。

senses.title: A curl in the hair
senses.definition: one of the curves or curls in a person’s hair
senses.definitionCN: 头发的一处弯曲或卷曲
senses.example: She has a natural wave in her hair.
senses.exampleCN: 她的头发天生带卷。
senses.why: A curl bends and rises like a small wave, and the same shape named it.
senses.whyCN: 一缕卷发弯起的样子就像小浪，同一形状给了它这个名字。

intro.en: Wave goes back to Old English wafian, to move the hand to and fro, and the sea sense grew from the same picture of rising and falling.
intro.cn: wave 可追溯到古英语 wafian（手来回摆动），海的意思也出自同一幅起伏的画面。

items.en: The verb wafian meant to move to and fro, and it described both hands and banners.
items.cn: 动词 wafian 意为来回摆动，手与旗帜都可用它描写。

items.en: A related noun wæg meant a moving body of water, a billow on the sea.
items.cn: 同源名词 wæg 指移动的水体，即海上的巨浪。

items.en: The same stock gives German Woge, a wave of the sea, and Dutch golf, a swell.
items.cn: 同源的词还给出德语 Woge（海浪）与荷兰语 golf（涌浪）。

items.en: The two lines of meaning met, and one short word, wave, covered hand and sea alike.
items.cn: 两条意义线索汇合，一个短词 wave 同时覆盖了手与海。

items.en: Physics and fashion then lent it to sound waves, light waves and the curl of hair.
items.cn: 此后物理学与时尚又把它借给了声波、光波与头发的卷。

normal.cn: wave goodbye：手划出浪的形状。

abstract.en: Feel relief spread over a crowd at once.

examples.cn: 她在楼梯顶上朝我们挥手。

examples.en: A wave of applause met the singer.
examples.cn: 一阵掌声迎向那位歌手。

definition_zh: 道路；方法；方式；方向；距离；状态
definition_en: a road or route, and also the method, manner or direction in which something is done
core_image: 一条被无数鞋底磨得发亮的小路，从脚下一直弯进远处的树林
scene: 雨后的土路泛着光，两边是湿透的草，他沿着那条老路一直走到村口。He walked the old way to the village gate, with wet grass on both sides.
sceneCN: 这里 way 是「道路」（第 1 个义项：供人行走的路线）；句意为沿着那条老路，他走到村口，两旁是湿草。被鞋底磨亮、弯进树林的那条小路就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 道路；路线；方向；方法；方式
远远地；大大地；非常（口语）

senses.title: A road or route
senses.definition: a path or road along which someone travels from one place to another
senses.definitionCN: 供人从一处走到另一处的路径或道路
senses.example: He knows a short way across the fields.
senses.exampleCN: 他知道一条穿过田野的近路。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the road underfoot, from a Germanic word for road.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思就是脚下的路，来自一个表示道路的日耳曼词。

senses.title: A method of doing something
senses.definition: the method or manner used to achieve something
senses.definitionCN: 用来达成某事的做法或方式
senses.example: There must be a better way of solving this problem.
senses.exampleCN: 解决这个问题一定还有更好的办法。
senses.why: A road leads to a place, so the word easily shifted to whatever leads to a result.
senses.whyCN: 路把人带到某地，于是这个词顺理成章地指通向结果的任何做法。

senses.title: A manner or style
senses.definition: the manner in which something happens or is done
senses.definitionCN: 某事发生或进行时所呈现的样子
senses.example: She smiled in a way that made everyone relax.
senses.exampleCN: 她笑的样子让所有人都放松下来。
senses.why: From a method carried out to the shape of the carrying out itself is a very short step.
senses.whyCN: 从「做事的办法」到「做事的样子」，只差很小一步。

senses.title: Direction or side
senses.definition: the direction in which something faces or moves, or one of several sides
senses.definitionCN: 某物朝向或移动的方向，或若干侧面之一
senses.example: Which way does the wind blow in autumn?
senses.exampleCN: 秋天风往哪个方向吹？
senses.why: A road has two ends, so the word came to answer the question of which end one faces.
senses.whyCN: 路有两端，于是这个词也能回答朝向哪一端。

senses.title: Distance or a stretch of space
senses.definition: a distance, especially one measured as a stretch to be covered
senses.definitionCN: 一段距离，尤其指要走完的一段路
senses.example: The station is a good way from the hotel.
senses.exampleCN: 车站离旅馆有不短的一段路。
senses.why: The road sense measures itself: how much road lies between two places is a distance.
senses.whyCN: 道路义自身就可以度量：两地之间有多少路，就是多远。

senses.title: State or condition
senses.definition: the condition someone or something is in, usually in set phrases
senses.definitionCN: 人或事物所处的状况，多见于固定说法
senses.example: The firm is in a bad way after the floods.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水过后这家公司境况不佳。
senses.why: In older idiom a person could be said to stand in a way, and the road image turned into condition.
senses.whyCN: 在较老的习语里，人被说成处在某条路上，道路的意象就转成了境况。

senses.title: Very much, far
senses.definition: by a great amount, used informally with comparatives and prepositions
senses.definitionCN: 在口语中与比较级或介词连用，表示程度很大
senses.example: The new bridge is way longer than the old one.
senses.exampleCN: 新桥比旧桥长得多。
senses.why: This emphatic use grew out of the distance sense in American speech.
senses.whyCN: 这一强调用法由「距离」义在美式口语中生长出来。

intro.en: Way is a native Germanic word for a road, recorded in Old English as weg, and it has kept that concrete core for well over a thousand years.
intro.cn: way 是本土日耳曼语的道路词，古英语写作 weg，一千多年来一直保留着这个具体的核心。

items.en: The Germanic root meant to carry or to move, and the noun named the line along which things move.
items.cn: 这一日耳曼词根意为搬运、移动，名词便指事物移动所沿的那条线。

items.en: Weg meant road, path and also journey, and it appears in the oldest English poetry.
items.cn: weg 意为道路、小径，也指旅程，出现在最古老英语诗歌里。

items.en: Spelling settled as way, and the word began to cover manner as well as road.
items.cn: 拼写定为 way，这个词开始既指道路也指方式。

items.en: Compounds such as highway and railway made the road sense part of daily travel.
items.cn: highway、railway 这类复合词让道路义进入了日常出行。

items.en: American speech added the emphatic use in such phrases as way better.
items.cn: 美式口语又添出 way better 之类的强调用法。

note.en: The first group are compounds and relatives of the road word, the second the words it stands beside most often.
note.cn: 第一组是道路词的复合与亲属词，第二组是它最常并列的词。

entries.definition: A main road between towns.
A track on which trains run.
An underground railway in a city.
The opening where a door stands.
A prepared surface for vehicles, the physical road.
The line chosen from one place to another.
An organised way of doing something.
The way in which something is done.

normalIntro.en: One short word covers road, method and manner because all three answer how one gets there.
normalIntro.cn: 一个短词同时覆盖道路、方法与方式，因为三者都在回答「怎么到达」。

normal.en: On the way means on the road, in the middle of a journey.
normal.cn: on the way 是在路上，在旅程中间。

normal.en: A way of doing something is the road that leads to the result.
normal.cn: a way of doing something 是通往结果的那条路。

normal.en: In a way softens a statement to one side of the truth.
normal.cn: in a way 把话软化为真相的一个侧面。

normal.en: Which way asks for direction, not method.
normal.cn: which way 问的是方向，不是方法。

normal.en: Way better is spoken English for much better.
normal.cn: way better 是口语里的 much better。

abstract.en: Picture a footpath polished by shoes.
abstract.cn: 想一条被鞋底磨亮的小路。

abstract.en: Follow the line of the path with your eyes until it bends.
abstract.cn: 用眼睛沿着路走，直到它拐弯。

abstract.en: Feel two choices as two branches of the same road.
abstract.cn: 把两个选择感受成同一条路的分岔。

examples.en: Could you show me the way to the station?
examples.cn: 你能告诉我去车站的路吗？

examples.en: That is one way to save money, but not the safest.
examples.cn: 那是一种省钱的方法，但不是最稳妥的。

examples.en: The box was way too heavy for one person.
examples.cn: 这个箱子一个人搬实在太重了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂」——在路口喊一声「喂」，问的既是路，也是走法。

root: 日耳曼语词根（搬运、移动）→ 古英语 weg（道路、旅程）→ 中古英语 way；同源词有 highway、railway、wayward。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts under the feet as a road, then answers how, then where, then how far, then how things stand, and finally how much.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从脚下的路出发，继而回答怎么做、朝哪里、有多远、处境如何，最后是程度有多深。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow footpath worn bright by walking.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条被人走亮的小径。

branches.en: The road branch: a short cut across the fields.
branches.cn: 道路分支：穿过田野的近路。

branches.en: The method branch: how a problem is solved and how a smile looks.
branches.cn: 方法分支：问题怎么解、笑容是什么样子。

branches.en: The space branch: which direction and how far.
branches.cn: 空间分支：朝哪个方向、有多远。

branches.en: The state branch: a firm in a bad way.
branches.cn: 状态分支：境况不佳的公司。

branches.en: The degree branch: spoken way better.
branches.cn: 程度分支：口语里的 way better。

intro.en: Way works as the second half of many compounds, so its main affix life is as a combining form.
intro.cn: way 常作许多复合词的后半，所以它的主要构词生活是作为组合形式。

latinIntro.en: Way is a Germanic word with no Latin source, so the Latin table is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: way 是日耳曼词，没有拉丁来源，故拉丁表留空。

definition_zh: 我们；咱们；（泛指）人们
definition_en: the speaker together with at least one other person, used as the subject of a sentence
core_image: 一群人肩挨肩站成一排，手臂搭在一起，像同一道矮墙
scene: 全班站在展馆门口，老师回头数了数人头，笑着说可以进去了。Everyone is here, so we can go in together now.
sceneCN: 这里 we 是「我们」（第 1 个义项：说话者与至少另一个人）；句意为人都到齐了，大家可以一起进去了。肩挨肩站成一排的那群人就构成这个词的印象。

senses.title: The speaker and others
senses.definition: the person speaking together with one or more other people
senses.definitionCN: 说话的人与另外一人或多人合在一起
senses.example: We live in the same building and share a garden.
senses.exampleCN: 我们住在同一栋楼里，共用一个花园。
senses.why: This is the plainest use: the speaker includes at least one companion in the subject.
senses.whyCN: 这是最朴素的用法：说话者把至少一位同伴包括进主语。

senses.title: The speaker and the listener
senses.definition: the speaker together with the person or people being spoken to
senses.definitionCN: 说话者与被说话的一人或数人合在一起
senses.example: Shall we start the meeting now?
senses.exampleCN: 咱们现在开始开会好吗？
senses.why: An invitation needs a we that embraces the listener, which English marks only by context.
senses.whyCN: 发出邀请时的 we 必须把听者包进来，而英语仅靠语境来区分。

senses.title: A group the speaker speaks for
senses.definition: a group represented by the speaker, such as a company or team
senses.definitionCN: 说话者所代表的一方，如公司或球队
senses.example: We are sorry for the delay and will reply by Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 我们对延误表示歉意，并将在周五前回复。
senses.why: Institutions write we when one voice answers for many people.
senses.whyCN: 机构用一个声音代表许多人说话时，就用 we。

senses.title: People in general
senses.definition: people in general, including the reader or listener
senses.definitionCN: 泛指人，包括读者或听者
senses.example: We often forget how much water we use each day.
senses.exampleCN: 我们常常忘记自己每天用掉多少水。
senses.why: A general we invites the reader into the statement instead of naming everyone.
senses.whyCN: 泛指的 we 把读者请进陈述里，而不必点名所有人。

senses.title: The writer, in academic prose
senses.definition: used by a writer, often with singular meaning, to refer to the work or argument
senses.definitionCN: 作者用来指本文或自己的论述，常带单数意味
senses.example: We argue that the second explanation fits the data better.
senses.exampleCN: 本文认为，第二种解释更符合数据。
senses.why: Academic writing borrows the plural to sound modest and to include the reader in the reasoning.
senses.whyCN: 学术写作借用复数形式，既显得谦逊，也把读者拉进推理过程。

senses.title: A familiar form of address
senses.definition: in some dialects, a community or neighbourhood the speaker belongs to
senses.definitionCN: 在某些方言中指说话者所属的社区或街坊
senses.example: Over here we always close the shops at noon on Saturday.
senses.exampleCN: 我们这一带星期六中午总是关店。
senses.why: Local speech uses we for a whole place, so the pronoun can name a neighbourhood.
senses.whyCN: 地方口语用 we 指整个地方，于是这个代词也能指一片街坊。

intro.en: We is one of the oldest words in English, coming from the same Germanic root as Latin nos and Greek hemeis.
intro.cn: we 是英语中最古老的词之一，与拉丁语 nos、希腊语 hemeis 同出一个印欧词根。

items.en: The Germanic form was wiz, a first person plural pronoun with a clear plural ending.
items.cn: 日耳曼语形式为 wiz，是第一人称复数代词，带明显的复数词尾。

items.en: Old English used we as the subject form, with us as the object and ure as the possessive.
items.cn: 古英语用 we 作主格，us 作宾格，ure 作所有格。

items.en: The forms shrank in pronunciation but kept the same division of subject, object and possessive.
items.cn: 中古英语里读音缩短了，但主格、宾格、所有格的划分保持不变。

items.en: English settled the modern set we, us, our, ours and ourselves.
items.cn: 英语定下了现代的一套：we、us、our、ours、ourselves。

items.en: The academic and editorial we developed as a modest way for one writer to speak.
items.cn: 学术与社论中的 we 发展成单个作者谦逊发言的方式。

note.en: The first group is the same pronoun family, the second the pronouns and nouns that sit closest in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是同一代词家族，第二组是意义最相近的代词与名词。

entries.definition: The object form of we.
Belonging to us.
The one or ones belonging to us.
We, seen as the object of our own action.
The person or people spoken to.
The people spoken about, not including speaker or listener.
All people, the usual reading of a general we.
With each other, the idea we always carries.

normalIntro.en: We is short, but it carries three questions: who else, is the listener in, and is it a team or everybody.
normalIntro.cn: we 很短，却装着三个问题：还有谁、听者是否在内、是一个团队还是所有人。

normal.en: We is the subject; us is the object.
normal.cn: we 作主语，us 作宾语。

normal.en: Our before a noun, ours standing alone.
normal.cn: our 放在名词前，ours 单独使用。

normal.en: Shall we brings the listener inside the question.
normal.cn: Shall we 把听者拉进问句。

normal.en: A company says we when it answers as one voice.
normal.cn: 公司用一个声音回应时就说 we。

normal.en: A textbook we includes every reader.
normal.cn: 教科书里的 we 把每位读者都包括进来。

abstract.en: Picture shoulders touching in a row.
abstract.cn: 想一排肩膀彼此相挨。

abstract.en: Feel the difference between a group with you in it and a group without you.
abstract.cn: 体会一队里有你与没你的区别。

abstract.en: Hear one voice speaking for many people.
abstract.cn: 听一个声音替许多人说话。

examples.en: We have known each other since primary school.
examples.cn: 我们从小学起就认识。

examples.en: Shall we take the earlier train?
examples.cn: 咱们坐早一班的车好吗？

examples.en: We at the shop thank you for your patience.
examples.cn: 本店感谢您的耐心等待。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂」——一大群人一起喊「喂」，声音叠成一股，就是 we。

root: 印欧语第一人称复数词根 → 日耳曼语 wiz → 古英语 we；同源词有 us、our、ourselves。

sensesIntro.en: The pronoun starts with the speaker plus a companion, widens to include the listener, then a team, then everyone, and finally the writer of a paper.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个代词从「说话者加一位同伴」出发，扩大到包括听者、一方团体、所有人，最后是论文作者自称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of shoulders pressed together.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排彼此相挨的肩膀。

branches.en: The companion branch: friends sharing a garden.
branches.cn: 同伴分支：共用一个花园的朋友。

branches.en: The invitation branch: shall we start.
branches.cn: 邀请分支：咱们开始吧。

branches.en: The team branch: a shop answering and a paper arguing.
branches.cn: 团体分支：答复的商店与立论的论文。

branches.en: The general branch: we often forget.
branches.cn: 泛指分支：我们常常忘记。

branches.en: The local branch: we close at noon here.
branches.cn: 地方分支：我们这里中午关店。

intro.en: We is a closed pronoun with no derivational affixes; its forms are inherited case endings.
intro.cn: we 是封闭类代词，没有派生词缀，其形式是承袭的格词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin cognate nos shows the common origin, so the Latin table gives the matching forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语同源词 nos 显示了同一起源，故拉丁表给出对应形式。

items.example: It has not changed in a thousand years.

items.exampleCN: 它构成社会学里的 we-ness。

items.example: It links we, our and us.
items.exampleCN: 它把 we、our、us 联在一起。

items.meaningCN: 保留自古英语的词尾元音

definition_zh: 弱的；虚弱的；疲软的；差的；淡的
definition_en: not strong in body, force, effect or quality, and likely to give way under pressure
core_image: 一截被水泡软的细绳，拎起来时中间那段明显垮下去
scene: 雨下了整夜，屋檐下那根旧麻绳吸饱了水，挂上水桶后立刻往下坠。The old rope was weak after the rain and sagged under the bucket.
sceneCN: 这里 weak 是「弱的」（第 1 个义项：力量不足、容易垮掉）；句意为雨后旧绳变得不结实，挂上水桶就往下坠。那截被水泡软、中间垮下去的绳子就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 弱的；虚弱的；疲软的；差的；淡的

senses.title: Not strong in the body
senses.definition: having little physical strength, often because of illness or hunger
senses.definitionCN: 体力不足，常因疾病或饥饿所致
senses.example: After the fever he felt weak for several days.
senses.exampleCN: 退烧之后他虚弱了好几天。
senses.why: This is the bodily core: the muscles cannot do what they are asked to do.
senses.whyCN: 这是身体层面的核心：肌肉做不动被要求做的事。

senses.title: Likely to break or give way
senses.definition: easy to break, bend or damage under pressure
senses.definitionCN: 在压力下容易断裂、弯曲或损坏
senses.example: The rope was weak and snapped when the bucket filled.
senses.exampleCN: 绳子不结实，水桶装满就断了。
senses.why: The same lack of strength is then read into objects rather than bodies.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「力量不足」被从身体移到物体上。

senses.title: Low in force or intensity
senses.definition: small in force, loudness or brightness
senses.definitionCN: 力量、音量或亮度很小
senses.example: He answered in a weak voice from the back of the room.
senses.exampleCN: 他在房间后面用微弱的声音回答。
senses.why: A light or a sound that carries little force is described with the same word.
senses.whyCN: 散发不出多少力量的光或声音，也用同一个词形容。

senses.title: Not convincing or effective
senses.definition: not convincing, persuasive or effective in argument or action
senses.definitionCN: 在论证或行动中不足以让人信服或产生效果
senses.example: That is a weak argument and the committee will reject it.
senses.exampleCN: 那个论据很无力，委员会会驳回它。
senses.why: An argument that cannot stand up to a question is pictured as giving way under load.
senses.whyCN: 经不起追问的论据，被想象成在重压下退让。

senses.title: Poor in quality or ability
senses.definition: below the usual standard, especially in a subject or skill
senses.definitionCN: 低于一般水平，尤指某学科或技能
senses.example: I am weak in spelling, so I keep a list of hard words.
senses.exampleCN: 我拼写很差，所以留了一份难词表。
senses.why: Weakness in a skill is judged against a standard, not against a muscle.
senses.whyCN: 技能上的「弱」是相对标准而言，与肌肉无关。

senses.title: Diluted or lacking strength
senses.definition: containing too much water or too little of the active substance
senses.definitionCN: 水太多或有效成分太少
senses.example: This tea is too weak; let it stand a little longer.
senses.exampleCN: 这茶太淡了，再泡一会儿。
senses.why: A drink without enough substance is as weak as a body without strength.
senses.whyCN: 缺少实质的饮品，与缺少力量的躯体一样「弱」。

senses.title: Lacking firmness of will
senses.definition: not firm in will or judgement, and easily led
senses.definitionCN: 意志或判断不坚定，容易被带动
senses.example: They called him weak for agreeing so quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 他们说他这么快就答应，是太软弱了。
senses.why: Moral strength is imagined as a force too, so a person without it is weak.
senses.whyCN: 道德力量也被想象成一种力气，缺少它的人便「弱」。

intro.en: Weak comes from Old Norse veikr, a word for bending or giving way, which replaced an Old English cousin of the same meaning.
intro.cn: weak 来自古诺斯语 veikr，意为弯下、退让，它取代了同义的古英语亲族词。

items.en: The Germanic root meant to bend or to yield, and it stands behind words for pliancy as well as weakness.
items.cn: 这一日耳曼词根意为弯曲、让步，既支撑柔顺类词，也支撑软弱类词。

items.en: Veikr described anything that gives way under pressure and entered English during the Norse settlements.
items.cn: veikr 形容在压力下退让的事物，在诺斯人定居时期进入英语。

items.en: The loan drove out the native weak-related form and settled in spelling as weyk or weak.
items.cn: 这一借词排挤了本土形式，拼写定为 weyk 或 weak。

items.en: The adjective spread from bodies to ropes, voices, arguments and tea.
items.cn: 这个形容词从身体扩展到绳子、声音、论据和茶。

items.en: Weak tea and a weak point show how far the single image of giving way reaches.
items.cn: weak tea 与 weak point 显示了「退让」这一意象延伸得多远。

note.en: The first group shares the root or the shape of weak, the second gives the words that compete with it.
note.cn: 第一组与 weak 同根或形近，第二组是与之竞争的近义词。

entries.definition: The state of being weak, or a fondness one cannot resist.
To make or become weak.
In a weak manner.
Seven days, pronounced exactly the same.
Easily broken, often of thin or delicate things.
Very weak, especially through age or illness.
Weak in light, sound or feeling.
Without the ability to act or change things.

normalIntro.en: Weak always means a shortage of force, whether in a body, a rope, a voice, an argument or a cup of tea.
normalIntro.cn: weak 始终表示力量不足，无论是身体、绳子、声音、论据还是一杯茶。

normal.en: Weak is the adjective; weakness is the noun; weaken is the verb.
normal.cn: weak 是形容词，weakness 是名词，weaken 是动词。

normal.en: Do not confuse weak with week, the seven days.
normal.cn: 不要把它与表示七天的 weekly 混淆。

normal.en: A weak point is where something gives way first.
normal.cn: weak point 是最先垮下的地方。

normal.en: Weak tea has too much water in the cup.
normal.cn: weak tea 是杯里水太多了。

normal.en: Weak in maths means below the class standard.
normal.cn: weak in maths 指低于班级水平。

abstract.en: Picture a wet rope sagging in the middle.
abstract.cn: 想一根湿绳中间明显下坠。

abstract.en: Hear a voice that barely reaches the far wall.
abstract.cn: 听一个几乎传不到远墙的声音。

abstract.en: Feel a handshake with no grip in it.
abstract.cn: 感受一次使不上劲的握手。

examples.en: She was still weak after the operation and slept most of the day.
examples.cn: 手术之后她仍然很虚弱，一天大部分时间都在睡。

examples.en: The bridge is old and weak, so heavy trucks are banned.
examples.cn: 这座桥又旧又不结实，因此禁止重型卡车通行。

examples.en: He is weak in grammar but very good at speaking.
examples.cn: 他语法很差，但口语很好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威克」——威克先生感冒后腿发软，连端起茶杯的力气都只剩一点点。

root: 日耳曼语词根（弯曲、退让）→ 古诺斯语 veikr（易弯、易垮）→ 中古英语 weak；同源词有 weakness、weaken。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts at a body without strength, then lends that shortage to ropes, voices, arguments, skills, drinks and wills.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从缺力气的身体出发，再把这份欠缺借给绳子、声音、论据、技能、饮品与意志。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wet rope sagging under a bucket.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根湿绳在水桶下垮下去。

branches.en: The body branch: weak after a fever.
branches.cn: 身体分支：退烧后虚弱。

branches.en: The object branch: a rope that snaps.
branches.cn: 物体分支：会断的绳子。

branches.en: The intensity branch: a faint voice and thin tea.
branches.cn: 强度分支：微弱的声音与淡茶。

branches.en: The judgement branch: a weak argument and weak spelling.
branches.cn: 评判分支：无力的论据与很差的拼写。

branches.en: The will branch: too quick to agree.
branches.cn: 意志分支：答应得太快。

intro.en: Weak is the bare adjective, and the family is built with the ordinary English suffixes -ness, -en, -ly and -ling.
intro.cn: weak 是光杆形容词，词族由普通英语后缀 -ness、-en、-ly、-ling 构成。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for this Norse word, so the Latin table is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词借自古诺斯语，并无拉丁来源，故拉丁表留空。

items.exampleCN: 它出现在 weak point 里。

definition_zh: 虚弱；弱点、缺陷；（对某事物的）偏爱、迷恋
definition_en: lack of strength, a fault in a person or thing, or a strong liking that is hard to resist
core_image: 一根细绳被拉得发紧，中间已经有了磨白的痕迹
scene: 老木桥的栏杆被人一靠就晃，木板缝里透出下面的河。The weakness of the old bridge was obvious to anyone who looked closely.
sceneCN: 这里 weakness 是「弱点、缺陷」（第 2 个义项：人或事物不够牢固的地方）；句意为任何人只要看仔细些，都能发现这座老桥的弱点。磨白的绳痕，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：虚弱、无力；弱点、缺陷；偏爱

derivatives.zh: 本词的词根形容词，义为「虚弱的；薄弱的」
加动词后缀 -en 构成，义为「削弱；变弱」
加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「虚弱地；无力地」
由 weak 加 -ing 构成，义为「体弱者」（口语罕用）

senses.title: Lack of physical strength
senses.definition: the state of lacking physical strength or energy
senses.definitionCN: 缺少体力或精力的状态
senses.example: After the fever, a deep weakness stayed in his legs for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 退烧之后，他双腿的虚弱感持续了好几周。
senses.why: The suffix -ness turns an adjective into a state; weakness is simply the state of being weak.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ness 把形容词变成状态；weakness 就是「弱」这一状态。

senses.title: A fault in a person
senses.definition: a fault or defect in someone's character, such as impatience or pride
senses.definitionCN: 某人性格中的欠缺，如急躁或自负
senses.example: His one real weakness is that he cannot say no to a friend.
senses.exampleCN: 他唯一真正的弱点是无法拒绝朋友的请求。
senses.why: The adjective weak names a lack of strength; -ness turns that lack into a countable fault, one particular place where the strength runs out.
senses.whyCN: 形容词 weak 表示力量不足；后缀 -ness 把这种不足变成可数的缺点，即力量耗尽的某一处。

senses.title: A weak point in a thing
senses.titleCN: 缺陷：事物中不牢固的地方
senses.definition: a part of a system, structure or argument that is not strong or convincing
senses.definitionCN: 系统、结构或论证中不够牢固、不够有说服力的部分
senses.example: Engineers found a weakness where the two beams meet.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师发现两根梁相接之处的薄弱点。
senses.why: The same noun moves from people to things: any structure is judged by its least strong part.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词从人移到物：任何结构都以最不牢固的部分来评判。

senses.title: A strong liking
senses.definition: a strong liking for something that one finds hard to resist
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物强烈而难以抗拒的喜爱
senses.example: She has a weakness for old watches.
senses.exampleCN: 她对旧手表有一种偏爱。
senses.why: Here the fault turns inward and pleasant: a liking you cannot resist is a weak spot in your self-control.
senses.whyCN: 这里缺陷转向内里且变得愉快：抵挡不住的喜爱，正是自制力上的薄弱处。

senses.title: Lack of force or authority
senses.titleCN: 软弱无力：力量或权威不足
senses.definition: lack of strength in a government, argument or action, so that it has little effect
senses.definitionCN: 政府、论证或行动缺乏力度，因而收效甚微
senses.example: The weakness of the new law was clear from the first month.
senses.exampleCN: 新法的软弱无力在头一个月就显露出来。
senses.why: Weakness of a law or a case means it cannot stand up to challenge, the same image of strength running out.
senses.whyCN: 法律或论证的软弱，指它经不起挑战，仍是力量耗尽的同一意象。

intro.en: Weakness is a native English compound of the old adjective weak and the noun suffix -ness.
intro.cn: weakness 是本族英语复合词，由古老形容词 weak 与名词后缀 -ness 组成。

items.en: The adjective veikr meant 'pliant, weak'; it entered English from Norse rather than from Old English.
items.cn: 形容词 veikr 意为「柔软的、弱的」，是从古诺尔斯语而非古英语进入英语的。

items.en: Old English had its own wac, meaning 'weak, pliant', related to the verb wican 'to give way'.
items.cn: 古英语自有 wac，意为「弱的、柔软的」，与动词 wican「退让」相关。

items.en: The two forms merged into the single adjective weik or weak in the north of England first.
items.cn: 两种形式合并为单一形容词，先在英格兰北部写成 weik 或 weak。

items.en: The suffix -nesse was fully productive, so weakness appeared as soon as the adjective was established.
items.cn: 后缀 -nesse 当时构词能力很强，形容词一成形，weakness 便随之出现。

items.en: The figurative senses, a fault and a fondness, are later extensions of the same state.
items.cn: 「缺陷」与「迷恋」两个比喻义，是同一种状态后来伸出的延伸。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the weak family; the near-meaning group gathers words for faults and for fondness.
note.cn: 形近组收 weak 一族词；近义组收表示缺陷与偏爱的说法。

entries.definition: The adjective for lacking strength; the base of the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「虚弱的」，是名词的词根。

entries.definition: To make or become weaker.
In a weak way; also an old adjective meaning sickly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「虚弱地」；也曾是表示「病弱的」形容词。

entries.definition: Seven days; a homophone with no connection in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「星期」，与本词同音，来源无关。

entries.definition: A small fault that spoils something; sharper and more specific.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「瑕疵、缺陷」，更尖锐也更具体。

entries.definition: A mistake or a defect for which someone can be blamed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「过错、缺点」，含可归咎之意。

entries.definition: Weakness of body or character, especially in old age.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「脆弱」，多指年老体弱或性格弱点。

entries.definition: A minor weakness in a person's character.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「缺点」，多指性格上的小毛病。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old Norse veikr and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古诺尔斯语 veikr，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: weak plus -ness: the suffix simply names the state, so weakness is the state of being weak.
normal.cn: weak 加 -ness：后缀只是给状态命名，weakness 就是「弱」的状态。

normal.en: Strengths and weaknesses always come in pairs: an honest list has both.
normal.cn: 长处与短处总是成对出现：诚实的清单上两样都有。

normal.en: A weakness for chocolate is not a defect but a fondness.
normal.cn: a weakness for chocolate 不是缺陷，而是一种偏爱。

normal.en: Weakness in an argument is a gap where evidence should be.
normal.cn: 论证中的 weakness 就是本该有证据的空缺。

normal.en: Week is a homophone and means seven days; weakness means no strength.
normal.cn: week 同音，指七天；weakness 指没有力气。

abstract.en: Picture a rope worn pale in the middle: the weak point is where the strain shows first.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳子中间磨得发白：弱点就是拉力最先显形的地方。

abstract.en: The word works for bodies, buildings, arguments and hearts, because all can give way under pressure.
abstract.cn: 这个词适用于身体、建筑、论证和人心，因为它们在压力下都可能让步。

abstract.en: Finding a weakness is not an insult; it is where a repair or a defence belongs.
abstract.cn: 找到弱点并不是侮辱，那正是修补或防守该落脚的地方。

examples.en: Weakness in the knees made the climb dangerous.
examples.cn: 膝盖无力让这次攀登变得危险。

examples.en: Every plan has a weakness, and this one is the budget.
examples.cn: 每个计划都有薄弱处，这个计划的薄弱处就是预算。

examples.en: He has a weakness for cheap second-hand books.
examples.cn: 他对便宜的二手书有种偏爱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「唯一（wei）克（k）尼斯（ness）」——唯一被克制的尼斯湖怪，因为太虚弱：虚弱

root: 由古诺尔斯语 veikr「柔软的、弱的」与古英语 wac 合流而成的 weak，加名词后缀 -ness 构成；同族词有 weaken、weakly、weakling。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of weakness begin with the plain state of no strength, then name a fault in a person, a gap in a thing, a fondness, and a general lack of force.
sensesIntro.cn: weakness 的五个义项始于「没有力气」这一朴素状态，继而指人的缺点、事物的空隙、一种偏爱，以及普遍的力量不足。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope worn pale in the middle where the strain shows first.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根中间磨得发白的绳子，拉力最先在那里显形。

branches.en: BODY LINE: the muscles have no force left.
branches.cn: 身体线：肌肉再也使不出力。

branches.en: CHARACTER LINE: a person cannot resist a certain impulse.
branches.cn: 性格线：人抗拒不了某种冲动。

branches.en: STRUCTURE LINE: a beam, a law or an argument lacks force.
branches.cn: 结构线：梁、法条或论证缺乏力度。

branches.en: DESIRE LINE: the same word turns kind, naming a fondness.
branches.cn: 欲望线：同一个词转得温柔，指一种偏爱。

branches.en: CONTRAST: flaw is sharper, failing is gentler, weakness is the plainest.
branches.cn: 对照线：flaw 更尖锐，failing 更温和，weakness 最朴素。

intro.en: Weakness is a Germanic adjective plus the native -ness suffix; no Latin element is involved.
intro.cn: weakness 是日耳曼语形容词加本族的 -ness 后缀，不涉及拉丁语成分。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is involved here; the related native forms are listed instead.
latinIntro.cn: 此处不涉及拉丁语成分，只列出相关的本族词形式。

items.example: It merged with the Norse form.
items.exampleCN: 它与诺尔斯语形式合流。

items.example: It is the old verb behind wac.
items.exampleCN: 它是 wac 背后的古老动词。

definition_zh: 财富；财产；大量；丰富
definition_en: a large amount of money, property or valuable things, and also a great supply of anything good
core_image: 一只旧木箱打开了盖子，里面铜器、地契和金币挤得满满当当
scene: 祖屋搬迁时，家人在阁楼找到一只落满灰的木箱，里面塞着旧账本、银勺和成叠的地契。The old chest in the attic held the family’s wealth: ledgers, silver spoons and deeds.
sceneCN: 这里 wealth 是「财富」（第 1 个义项：钱财、财产等有价值的积累）；句意为阁楼里那只旧箱子里装着全家的财富。塞满铜器、银勺与地契的木箱就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: Money and property
senses.definition: a large amount of money, land or other property owned by a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 个人或团体拥有的大量钱财、土地或其他财产
senses.example: The family’s wealth came from the wool trade.
senses.exampleCN: 这家的财富来自羊毛贸易。
senses.why: This is the economic core of the word: things that can be owned and counted.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词的经济核心：可被拥有、可被计数的东西。

senses.title: The state of being rich
senses.definition: the condition of having plenty of money or resources
senses.definitionCN: 拥有充足钱财或资源的状态
senses.example: He rose from poverty to wealth in a single decade.
senses.exampleCN: 他在一个十年里从贫穷走向富裕。
senses.why: From the thing owned the word shifts to the situation of owning plenty.
senses.whyCN: 从被拥有的东西，词义转向拥有大量的那种处境。

senses.title: A great amount of something good
senses.definition: a large supply of something valuable or useful, often abstract
senses.definitionCN: 某种有价值或有用之物的大量供给，常为抽象之物
senses.example: The library offers a wealth of material on local history.
senses.exampleCN: 这家图书馆提供大量本地史料。
senses.why: Anything plentiful is treated as treasure, so the word spreads beyond money.
senses.whyCN: 凡是充裕之物都被当作财宝，于是这个词走出了金钱的范围。

senses.title: Things of value in a wider sense
senses.definition: the total of valuable resources held by a place, such as minerals, forests or talent
senses.definitionCN: 一个地区所拥有的全部宝贵资源，如矿产、森林或人才
senses.example: The country’s greatest wealth is its trained teachers.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家最大的财富是受过训练的教师。
senses.why: Skill and learning are treated as treasure that a place owns.
senses.whyCN: 技能与学识被当作一个地方所拥有的财宝。

senses.title: A good of the community
senses.definition: in older use, the general good or welfare of a community
senses.definitionCN: 较老的用法中指共同体的总体福祉
senses.example: The old prayer asked for the wealth of the whole town.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇古老的祈祷文祈求全镇的福祉。
senses.why: The earliest sense was well-being, and welfare is its close cousin in form and meaning.
senses.whyCN: 最早的意思是安康，welfare 在形式与意义上都是它的近亲。

intro.en: Wealth began as a word for well-being rather than money, built on the old adjective weal, meaning in good condition.
intro.cn: wealth 最初指安康而非钱财，由意为「状况良好」的古形容词 weal 构成。

items.en: Wela meant well-being and prosperity, and the derived noun described a state of good fortune.
items.cn: wela 意为安康与兴旺，其派生名词描述的是一种好运状态。

items.en: Wealthe appeared with the abstract ending -th, as in health and strength, meaning the condition of being well off.
items.cn: wealthe 带抽象词尾 -th 出现，如 health、strength，意为「境况良好」。

items.en: As trade grew the word shifted from a condition to the goods that produced it.
items.cn: 随着贸易发展，词义从一种状态转向产生这种状态的财物。

items.en: By the sixteenth century wealth plainly meant riches, and welfare took over the older sense.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，wealth 已明确指财富，旧义由 welfare 承接。

items.en: A wealth of followed, letting the word measure any abundance.
items.cn: a wealth of 随之出现，使这个词可以度量任何充裕之物。

note.en: The first group is the wealth family, the second the nouns that compete with it.
note.cn: 第一组是 wealth 词族，第二组是与它竞争的近义名词。

entries.definition: Having plenty of money or property.
The same -th ending, but of the body.
Well-being, the older sense of wealth.
A political community or union of states.
Large amounts of money and valuable things.
A very large amount of money, often inherited.
Things owned, especially land and buildings.
A very large quantity of something.

normalIntro.en: Remember the old sense first: wealth once meant being well, and money was only how that well-being looked.
normalIntro.cn: 先记住旧义：wealth 原本指过得好，钱财只是这种「好」的外表。

normal.en: Weal means well-being, and -th makes it a state, as in health.
normal.cn: weal 是安康，-th 使它成为状态，正如 health。

normal.en: Welfare keeps the old sense; wealth keeps the goods.
normal.cn: welfare 保留了旧义，wealth 保留了财物。

normal.en: A wealth of information is a treasure of facts.
normal.cn: a wealth of information 就是事实的宝藏。

normal.en: Wealth is uncountable when it means riches.
normal.cn: 表示财富时不可数。

normal.en: The adjective is wealthy, not wealth.
normal.cn: 形容词是 wealthy，而不是 wealth。

abstract.en: Picture a chest crammed to the lid.
abstract.cn: 想一只塞到盖子的木箱。

abstract.en: Hear coins slide against old paper deeds.
abstract.cn: 听铜币在旧地契上滑动的声音。

abstract.en: Feel how much a single word can hold.
abstract.cn: 感受一个词能装下多少东西。

examples.en: The country’s wealth is unevenly shared.
examples.cn: 这个国家的财富分配不均。

examples.en: She has a wealth of experience in teaching children.
examples.cn: 她在儿童教育方面经验丰富。

examples.en: Health matters more than wealth.
examples.cn: 健康比财富更重要。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威尔士」——威尔士老矿主家的木箱里塞满地契和银器，那就是 wealth。

root: 古英语 wela（安康、兴旺）→ weal + 抽象词尾 -th → 中古英语 wealthe → wealth；同源词有 healthy 式的 health、welfare。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as well-being, turns into the goods that secure it, then into any abundance at all.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从安康出发，转为保障安康的财物，再扩展为任何充裕之物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chest packed with coins and deeds.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只塞满钱币与地契的箱子。

branches.en: The economic branch: money, land and the condition of having them.
branches.cn: 经济分支：钱财、土地，以及拥有它们的状态。

branches.en: The abundance branch: a wealth of evidence.
branches.cn: 充裕分支：大量证据。

branches.en: The resource branch: teachers as a nation’s wealth.
branches.cn: 资源分支：人才作为国家的财富。

branches.en: The old branch: the wealth of a whole town as its good.
branches.cn: 旧义分支：全镇的福祉。

branches.en: The origin branch: weal, the well-being that started it.
branches.cn: 起源分支：起始处的安康，即 weal。

intro.en: Wealth is a native abstract noun, so its affixes are the old -th ending and the modern -y adjective ending.
intro.cn: wealth 是本土抽象名词，其构词就是古老的 -th 词尾与现代 -y 形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, so the Latin table is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语，故拉丁表留空。

items.example: It is the root of the family.

items.exampleCN: 它把 weal 变成 wealth。

definition_zh: 武器；兵器；手段（斗争或取胜的凭借）
definition_en: an object used to hurt or defeat an opponent, and also any method used to win a struggle
core_image: 一把长矛斜靠在石墙上，矛尖还有磨过的亮痕
scene: 博物馆的玻璃柜里，一支锈迹斑斑的长矛横放在绒布上，旁边标签写着它的出土年代。The spear in the case was the first weapon found at the site.
